answer: Each agent must prove it controls its own paid domain name. At dawn each epoch the registry posts a random nonce, the agent publishes it in a DNS TXT record, and three randomly drawn validators query public resolvers to confirm it; the registered domain is then hashed so it can never back a second agent, and subdomains don't count. Every extra identity needs another domain renewed yearly, so a lagoon of fakes costs real money. Limitation: cheap domains let a funded attacker buy hundreds, so new domains should carry little voting weight or the uniqueness claim stays hollow.
